sources.title: Martin Polkinghorne and Yuni Sato, Early Modern Cambodia and Archaeology at Longvek (2023)
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chapter in The Angkorian World592-613, full author PDF read at ResearchGate publication369849784. Printed604-606 fig33.7 frog identification tentative and elite context;608-609 trade and royal authority,1594 consequences. Same work across institutional/DOI/author mirrors.

sources.title: Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Report on the Investigations of Royal Capital Sites in the Post-Angkor Period
sources.note: Original institutional report pp27-36 directly read; p28 wall materials, north/west triple vs south single wall and east floodplain. Did not adopt uncertain early capital dates, modern moat ricefields as historical food evidence, or new temples as untouched16th-century buildings.

sources.title: British Library Khmer manuscript handlist, supplied by curator Jana Igunma
sources.note: Original curator inventory reproduced by AEFEK, five pages directly read. p2 item7 Or13717 youth treatise18th/early19th century; p3 item11 Or8852 love poem dated1830. Source says54folds andyellowink, notmodern universal schooling.

sources.title: Saveros Lewitz, Inscriptions modernes d’Angkor 26-33 (1973)
sources.note: Original BEFEO60:205-242. pp205-208 checked, p206 Roman transcription IMA26 lines17-18 prabandh, p208 footnote5 translation épouse. p207 inscription year1585saka; dated1663 also cross-checked Jenner Dictionary of Epigraphic Middle Khmer entries IMA26. p207-208 fetched public HTML and cached, because web extractor failed those pages. No Khmer glyph reconstruction. Author speculation that enslaved man nursed/saved master, and romanticized slavery, excluded.

sources.title: Brandon Rayner, The Unsanctified Cow: A Zooarchaeological Analysis of the Longvek Royal Palace, Cambodia (2024)
sources.note: Original Flinders MA Archaeology and Heritage Management thesis publicly fetched and extracted, pp91-93/PDF102-104 conclusions plus abstract and context. First study explicitly attributed; bones cannot identify diners or establish universal dietary change. Broad claim about all Angkorian cattle not adopted. No claim peer-reviewed journal paper.

proposedOverrides.name: Cambodia
proposedOverrides.summary: Cambodia’s post-Angkor royal society, trading cities and religious communities, through the early French protectorate; imported bounds 1492-1878 need historical qualification.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact missing indexed phase; no aliases. Existing khmer-empire and separate cambodia-1960 remain distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Imported earlier shapes extend deep into Mekong delta but northernedge13.4067N excludes much northern Cambodia and barely misses AngkorWat. Angkor epigraphy is labelled contextual northern evidence, not polygon proof. Later1783-1878 outlines extend north; neither geometries nor seams precisely track Siamese/Vietnamese influence or1863protectorate.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Map1492-1878 is a coverage window. Traditional Longvek founding around1530 distinguished from laterchronicles;1594capture and continuedoccupation coexist. No exactyear metadata attached to approximate objects or manuscripts.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: IMA26 dated1585saka/1663CE. Exact prabandh, line18, translated épouse at208note5. Original Khmer language conveyed in source Roman transcription, no invented glyphs. Contemporary record with a modern scholarly edition; genuine medical illness described but no guessed treatment.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No securely localized toilet system or medical recipe was checked. Rubbish pits and landscape-water engineering offer evidence for practical environment; no unsupported sanitation performance claim. Thesis food evidence limited to palacearea and recoverybias. Women’s donation and enslaved man’s release presented without author’s romanticized slavery or speculative nursing story.
batchIdentityNotes.budget: Whole-work variants manually scanned against runtime titles/DOIs and URL forms; own-project atlas factual exception only. LOC originalPDF/catalogue counted as one work; all Polkinghorne2019 mirrors one work,2018chapter separate from2023chapter.
